text: A firewall rule and a VNet service endpoint both narrow who can reach Azure SQL's public endpoint — neither removes it. A Private Endpoint does: a private IP inside your own VNet, powered by Azure Private Link.
Creating a Private Endpoint is a connection request, not something automatic from one side alone. Before approval, it sits Pending — traffic isn't flowing yet.
Once someone with the right permission on the Azure SQL server approves it, the connection flips to Approved and the private IP path goes live. That approval step is itself a security control.
A private IP only helps if DNS actually resolves to it. Skip the privatelink.database.windows.net zone, and clients keep resolving to the public IP, silently bypassing the private path.

Private Endpoints are the strongest network control in this chapter, but cost setup complexity and real network line-of-sight for every client. Next up: when public-with-a-firewall is enough, and when it isn't.
